title: Query Understanding: Spelling, Intent & Filters
interviewAnswer: Search quality often improves before retrieval by normalizing queries, correcting spelling, identifying entities/intent and extracting structured filters. Query rewriting must preserve user intent.
keyPoints: Exact identifiers should not be “corrected” like prose.
why: Query Understanding: Spelling, Intent & Filters is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
intuition: Exact identifiers should not be “corrected” like prose.
deepDive: Search quality often improves before retrieval by normalizing queries, correcting spelling, identifying entities/intent and extracting structured filters. Query rewriting must preserve user intent. Filters can improve precision dramatically. Log query reformulations as feedback. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Parse “red M8 bolt 50mm” into lexical terms plus product/color/size filters.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Query Understanding: Spelling, Intent & Filters have?

production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
